subject: Eval roadmap -> capacity commitment: discount ladder & burst cap discussion
messages:
From: Elliot Grant <elliot@ai-innovations.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot evaluation & reserved capacity — request for MAP + pricing

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and KV-cache behavior looked promising for our user flows. We'd like to formalize a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so our PM/infra teams can sign off on an evaluation and understand how a Dedicated capacity reservation could work. Key asks from our side:

- A staged evaluation timeline (pilot -> canary -> prod) with clear acceptance gates
- Proposed GPU-pool sizing for the pilot and ramp targets for 6 / 12 months
- Pricing tiers tied to committed capacity (we're interested in a discount ladder depending on term and committed GPUs)
- Burst clauses and overage rates — we prefer a soft cap on burst charges during the pilot
- A rough SOW and expected close timeline if we hit the milestones

Could you send a draft MAP and a pricing ladder we can take to procurement? Procurement will want capped worst-case monthly charges for the pilot so they can approve the PoC budget.

Best,
Elliot Grant
Head of Research
AiInnovate Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation & reserved capacity — request for MAP + pricing

Elliot — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a pricing ladder spreadsheet (high-level). High level summary below and callouts you can take to procurement:

Attachment stubs:
- AiInnovate_MAP_v0.1.pdf (MAP outline: milestones, owners, exit criteria)
- pricing-ladder.xlsx (commit vs monthly rate vs discounts)
- SOW-draft-AIInnovate.docx (placeholder SOW)

MAP highlights (short):
- Pilot (4 weeks): 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, 25k token/day expected peak, engineering acceptance test (latency P50 < 90ms, P95 < 220ms)
- Canary (8 weeks after pilot): 8 x GPUs reserved, KV-prefix cache enabled; throughput validation + ops runbook
- Prod ramp (month 3-12): step-up to 24 x GPUs by month 6 if acceptance gates met

Pricing ladder (example):
- 1 quarter (3mo) minimum: base rate $X per GPU/hr (pilot pricing)
- 6 month commit: 8% discount vs base
- 12 month commit: 15% discount + 2% credit for early payment
- 24 month commit: 22% discount + optional price protection clause

Burst clauses (proposal):
- Soft burst allowance during pilot: up to 30% additional capacity without immediate charges, billed as usage with a 50% surcharge if sustained >72 hours
- For committed tiers, bursts up to 2x reserved for short windows (bound to escalation policy); sustained bursts convert to temporary overage billing or automated auto-scale (if enabled)

Procurement-friendly items included in PDF: worst-case pilot invoice cap (based on X hours/month at pilot footprint), sample SLA credits, and a stub for security/compliance attachments.

Next steps:
1) You and procurement review the MAP + pricing spreadsheet — call out any hard caps you need on the pilot.
2) We iterate (Marissa will own contract points).
3) Aim to sign pilot SOW by May 18 so we can kick pilot the week of May 24.

If useful, happy to schedule a call with our delivery/ops lead to walk through burst behavior and billing.

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Elliot / Ben — quick operational notes from the delivery side:

- Pilot sizing: recommend we add a small buffer to the pilot GPUs (e.g., 2 -> 3 GPUs) so the pilot can exercise eviction/burst scenarios without immediate throttling. This reduces false negatives in acceptance testing.
- SLA & burst: suggest defining a "pilot protection band" — a fixed $ cap on burst charges for the pilot month (e.g., $5k) and a clear definition of "sustained burst" ( > 72h average at >125% of reserved).
- Invoicing: for pilots we'll issue at most two invoices (start and consolidated usage) so procurement has predictability.
- Security/Compliance: we'll attach SOC2 evidence and a short data-flow diagram to the MAP PDF.

I've annotated the MAP PDF with these operational points (see AiInnovate_MAP_v0.1.pdf). Vivek — any comments on kernel/quantization recommendations we should propose for the pilot to reduce token cost?

Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@ai-innovations.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation & reserved capacity — request for MAP + pricing

Marissa / Ben — procurement here. A few redlines / clarifying asks before legal will accept the PoC SOW: 

1) Pilot invoice cap: we need a hard cap on the pilot month (not just an estimate). Can you provide a firm dollar cap for the pilot (assuming 3 GPUs and worst-case 720 hours)?
2) Burst surcharge cap: the 50% surcharge is okay, but we want a monthly maximum for burst charges (e.g., no more than 1.5x the committed monthly fee) during the pilot.
3) Termination for convenience: pilot should have a 7-day exit with pro-rated charges.
4) Data retention: confirm logs/audit retention for the pilot environment (30 days min; we may request 90 days).

If you can update the MAP/SOW with these items we can move the PoC approval through finance today.

Regards,
Procurement Team
AiInnovate Inc.

Thanks — good, actionable asks. Updated items below (we'll push a clean MAP + SOW revision by EOD):

1) Firm pilot cap: assuming 3 x A100-eq reserved for full month (720 hours) plus an assumed 48 hours of burst at 2x, firm cap = $18,500 for pilot month (this includes a capped burst allowance of $3,500).
2) Burst surcharge cap: during pilot, total monthly burst charges will be capped at 1.25x the committed monthly fee (we accept a lower cap than requested for pilot).
3) Termination: pilot term includes 7-day termination for convenience with pro-rated charges on committed capacity and no early-termination penalty.
4) Data retention: logs/audit retained 90 days for the pilot; we will provide SOC2 snippets in the MAP PDF.

Proposed close timeline:
- May 12: Procurement confirms acceptance of above caps and sends signed PO
- May 18: Pilot SOW signed by both parties
- Week of May 24: Pilot kickoff

I've also dropped a link to the HubSpot deal and the draft MAP in the shared drive. If procurement confirms the cap language we'll finalize the SOW and get legal looped.

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
